newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - API's bring distillate surprise--sort of.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - API's bring distillate surprise--sort of.

text.p: This week's report from the American Petroleum Institute brought an unexpected draw in distillate stocks, but a closer inspection reveals the drop may not be as bullish as it looks, traders said.
Also unexpected was the large 6.1 million barrel draw in crude oil stocks API showed related to a drop in imports.
NYMEX crude and heating oil rose in late trade on the ACCESS overnight trading system, while gasoline slipped after the report confirmed forecasts for a build in stocks.
Still some traders were taking a wait-and-see attitude.
Some traders were concerned that so many players were out of the trading fray and enjoying the back-to-back Christmas and New Years Day holidays.

"It's obviously real dead, so it's hard to get a good impression of the market's reaction to the report," a futures trader said. But other traders went farther saying even the thintalk could not long disguise the report's neutral flavor.

"Some may try to point to (the crude drop) and to distillates, but this market is trading on weather reports and I just don't see anything to hang my hat on," said Tom Knight, a refined products trader at Fina Inc in New Jersey.

Knight said that even though the 1.89 million barrel drop in overall distillate stocks disguised the fact that heating oil stocks actually rose by 284,000 barrels, the total stock drop was not big enough for the week before winter's start.
"The numbers are not significant," Knight said.
Some other traders also said reactions to the report could turn out bearish due to the heating oil build.

"It's not a big draw in distillates, and I could definitely see some negatives in the report," said Tom Bentz, director of the energy division at ING Derivatives Clearing, Inc. "But crude is strong, and heating oil is just following."
ACCESS traders pushed February crude up nearly 20 cents to $25.12 a barrel, with February heating oil in tow trading 0.45 cent higher at 70.55 cents a gallon.
But February gasoline dipped about 0.10 cent to 69.45 cents a gallon after API showed stocks building by 504,000 barrels to nearly 192 million barrels.
Crude stocks stood 292.9 million barrels, 21.9 million barrels below year-ago levels, while total distillates stood at 121.3 million, or 6.6 million barrels below a year ago.
